subject.title: La Mesa-Spring Valley School District Board, Trustee Area 1

text: I am a second-generation La Mesa-Spring Valley School District graduate and in the class of 2003 from Grossmont High School. My mother taught at Northmont Elementary before retiring. I received a Master’s Degree from Point Loma Nazarene University and have been teaching special education for nearly twenty years.

I am married to my high school sweetheart, and we are foster/adoptive/biological parents to 6 children, ranging in ages from 3 to 18. They are all current or future La Mesa-Spring Valley School District students or graduates and have a range of educational needs. Prior to serving on the school board, I was PTA president at my children’s elementary school, and I remain active in the PTA. My faith inspires me to act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly.

My purpose for being on the school board was and will continue to be to give back to the district and community that shaped me into who I am. I love collaboration and believe we are better humans when we surround ourselves with people who look, think, and act differently from us. I believe the top priority of a school district is to develop kind, hardworking, community- and service-oriented students. When La Mesa-Spring Valley School District thrives, my children thrive.

text: My name is Rebecca Drexler Tweedle and I am running for La Mesa Spring Valley School Board. I want to serve our community as a pragmatic champion of public education despite the current economic challenges it faces. A parent of two children in the LMSV school district, I have been actively involved by volunteering in their classrooms, school garden, starting a Run Club and volunteering in other extracurricular activities, including AYSO and little league.

A San Diego native, I have lived in La Mesa for 8 years and attended UCSD for undergrad. I have an MA in International Peace and Conflict Resolution and a Masters Certificate in International Development. My goals are to support and uplift our school district through quality public education at all our neighborhood schools.

My priorities include student safety and supporting student mental health. LMSV deserves high quality education through evidence-backed, modern methods. Our school district needs to promote competitive compensation for its teachers and staff in order to attract and retain high-quality personnel. I have been endorsed by the LMSV Teachers Association. To learn more, visit rebeccatweedle.com.
Please support our schools by voting for Rebecca Tweedle.
